articles.title: Bitcoin Falls Below $60,000 for the First Time Since July
articles.excerpt: Bitcoin traded near $59,500 at 11:51 a.m. ET Friday, down 5.5% in 24 hours, as AI stocks sold off and a crypto sentiment index sat at 12.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin fell below $60,000 on Friday for the first time since July, [Reuters reported](https://live.euronext.com/en/financial-news/bitcoin-falls-below-60000-level). It traded near $59,500 at 11:51 a.m. ET, down 5.5% over 24 hours, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

The drop puts bitcoin about 30% below where it stood 30 days ago, near $84,500 on Oct. 21, per CoinGecko data. Yahoo Finance data show the coin down 23% so far in November, which would be its worst month since June 2022, when it fell 38%, [Yahoo Finance reported](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/bitcoin-plunges-below-60000-on-pace-for-its-worst-month-since-june-2022-162908483.html).

**Tech stocks and fund exits**

Reuters tied the move to concerns about high valuations in the AI trade and other risk assets. Chip stocks fell Friday after Anthropic's Nasdaq debut, with Nvidia down about 3.8% and AMD about 5.1% at the time of [Decrypt's report](https://decrypt.co/383702/bitcoin-breaks-below-60k-crypto-fear-greed-index-lowest).

Ether traded near $1,643 at 11:51 a.m. ET, down 7.4% over 24 hours, per CoinGecko.

U.S. spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds lost $582.3 million on Thursday, taking November withdrawals to about $3.5 billion, according to [Farside Investors](https://farside.co.uk/btc/) data cited by Yahoo Finance.

**How the fear gauge works**

The Crypto Fear & Greed Index scores market mood from 0, extreme fear, to 100, extreme greed. It blends price swings, trading volume, social media activity and other market data. The [Alternative.me](https://alternative.me/crypto/fear-and-greed-index/) version stood at 12 on Friday, in its "Extreme Fear" band. A low reading describes mood; it does not predict the next move.

**The other view**

Fundstrat strategist Sean Farrell said Thursday that signs of a bottom were starting to emerge, but that selling had not yet reached past levels he would call compelling, Yahoo Finance reported.

*In our opinion: the number that matters is $3.5 billion, the November exit from U.S. bitcoin funds. It comes on top of a 30% price drop in 30 days, and the losses sit with fund holders as well as the miners and treasury companies that keep bitcoin on their books. Friday's flow figures from Farside Investors will show whether the exits slowed or sped up.*

articles.title: Hong Kong Bill Would Require Licenses for Four More Crypto Services
articles.excerpt: The Virtual Asset Services bill, gazetted Friday, would put crypto dealing, advice, management and custody under the SFC. First reading is Dec. 2.
articles.body_md:
Hong Kong published a bill on Friday, Nov. 20, that would require firms offering four more types of crypto services to be licensed by or registered with the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), the [government said](https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202611/20/P2026112000582.htm).

The Virtual Asset Services Legislation (Amendment) Bill 2026 covers dealing, advisory, asset management and custody services. Today, Hong Kong's anti-money-laundering law licenses only one crypto activity, running a trading platform, according to [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/policy/2026/11/20/hong-kong-moves-to-extend-crypto-licensing-rules-to-brokers-advisers-and-custodians) and [Caixin](https://finance.caixin.com/2026-11-20/102507342.html).

**What changes, and for whom**

The bill would amend the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance. Anyone running one of the four businesses in Hong Kong would need an SFC license or registration and would face a fit-and-proper test, a check of a firm's honesty, finances and competence.

Banks and stored-value facility licensees, such as e-wallet operators supervised by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), would also have to register with the SFC before offering crypto services. The bill gives the SFC and the HKMA powers to run the regime.

In plain terms, a custodian holds client crypto for safekeeping, a dealer buys and sells for clients, and an adviser recommends what to buy. Under the bill, each would need its own permission.

**Officials' case for the bill**

Financial Services Secretary Christopher Hui said the bill follows the principle of "same activity, same risks, same regulation." SFC chief executive Julia Leung said it "marks an important milestone in completing Hong Kong's regulatory framework for virtual assets."

The government's release did not say when the new licensing rules would take effect, and no industry response appeared in the reports Black Mint reviewed. The bill is a proposal and is not law yet.

*In our opinion: the question worth chasing is how long current firms get to comply. Brokers, fund managers and custodians already serving Hong Kong clients would need SFC sign-off, and banks would need a second regulator's registration on top of the HKMA. The Dec. 2 first reading in the Legislative Council is the first date on the calendar; transition terms are the detail to watch.*

articles.title: SEC Says Backward Hat Capital Raised $560 Million in Ponzi Scheme
articles.excerpt: The SEC won an asset freeze against the Indianapolis firm, which it says promised crypto-funded forex trading returning at least 6% a month. The CFTC also sued.
articles.body_md:
The Securities and Exchange Commission said Friday, Nov. 20, that it obtained a temporary restraining order and asset freeze against Indianapolis-based Backward Hat Capital, alleging the firm and its co-founders raised about $560 million from more than 2,000 investors in a Ponzi scheme, according to the [SEC's release](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2026-116-sec-charges-indianapolis-based-backward-hat-capital-its-co-founders-560-million-dollar-offering).

**What the complaint alleges**

The SEC says co-founders Phillip Williams and Devin Johnson told investors their money would be converted to crypto assets and used for foreign exchange (FX) arbitrage, run by an "AI-driven" algorithm they said returned at least 6% a month. Arbitrage means profiting from small price gaps between markets.

Instead, the complaint alleges, the defendants paid more than $250 million to earlier investors with newer investors' money and moved more than $220 million to themselves. That pattern is what makes a Ponzi scheme: returns paid from fresh deposits, not profits.

The SEC also charged Johnson's firm Traders Point Capital and Joseph Anderson, who it says produced fake "audit reports" for investors. The case was filed in federal court in the Southern District of Indiana.

**Parallel cases**

The Commodity Futures Trading Commission [filed its own complaint](https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/9328-26) alleging the scheme took in more than $550 million from at least 2,100 participants and did little, if any, forex trading. Federal prosecutors in Manhattan charged Williams and Johnson with securities fraud and conspiracy, and both were arrested on Nov. 18, the [IRS Criminal Investigation unit said](https://www.irs.gov/compliance/criminal-investigation/two-individuals-charged-in-600-million-ponzi-scheme).

The charges are allegations, and the defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty. Black Mint did not find a public response from the defendants or their lawyers in the filings or reports reviewed.

The SEC urged investors to use resources on [Investor.gov](https://www.investor.gov/) to check offers before investing.

*In our opinion: the stake is the money of more than 2,000 investors, and the asset freeze is what stands between them and further losses. Promised returns of 6% a month would more than double money in a year, the kind of figure the SEC's own warning flags. The next thing to watch is whether the Indiana court extends the temporary freeze into a longer-lasting order.*

articles.title: Bitcoin ETFs Lose $582.3 Million, Their Worst Day of November
articles.excerpt: BlackRock's IBIT accounted for $541.1 million of Thursday's exits, pushing November's net outflows from U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs to about $3.47 billion.
articles.body_md:
Investors pulled $582.3 million out of U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs on Thursday, the biggest one-day outflow of November, [Farside Investors data show](https://farside.co.uk/btc/). The month's net outflows now stand at about $3.47 billion across 14 trading days.

That is the third straight session of net selling, after $239.9 million on Tuesday and $306.5 million on Wednesday. Before Thursday, the worst day of the month was Nov. 5, at $430.2 million.

**IBIT carried most of Thursday's selling**

- BlackRock's IBIT: -$541.1 million
- Fidelity's FBTC: -$45.9 million
- ARK's ARKB: -$31.3 million
- Grayscale's GBTC: -$13.9 million
- MSBT: +$49.6 million

IBIT alone made up about 93% of the day's total. U.S. spot ether ETFs lost another $131.2 million on Thursday, $124.2 million of it from BlackRock's ETHA, according to [Farside's ether table](https://farside.co.uk/eth/).

**How the flow number works**

A spot bitcoin ETF holds real bitcoin for its shareholders. When investors redeem more shares than they buy, large brokers called authorized participants hand shares back, and the fund sells or delivers bitcoin to cover them. So an outflow means the fund's bitcoin pile got smaller. Farside tallies each fund's daily net flow in U.S. dollars.

**Prices on Friday morning**

Bitcoin traded near $62,050 at 5:55 a.m. ET Friday, down about 2.8% over 24 hours, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin). Ether was near $1,757, down about 2.6%. The [Crypto Fear & Greed Index](https://alternative.me/crypto/fear-and-greed-index/) read 12, in its "Extreme Fear" band.

Since launching in January 2024, the funds still show about $53.6 billion in net inflows by Farside's count.

*In our opinion: the number that matters is $541.1 million, because one fund did nearly all the selling on Thursday. Investors who hold bitcoin through a brokerage account have now taken out about $3.47 billion in November. Friday's flow figure is the next one to watch, with five trading days left in the month after it.*

articles.title: Senate Passes DEATH BETS Act to Ban War and Death Prediction Bets
articles.excerpt: The bill, passed by voice vote Thursday, would bar CFTC-registered exchanges from listing contracts tied to war, terrorism or a death. It now goes to the House.
articles.body_md:
The U.S. Senate on Thursday passed S. 4035, the DEATH BETS Act, a bill that would ban CFTC-registered exchanges from listing prediction market contracts tied to war, terrorism, assassination or a person's death. It passed by voice vote at 6:47 p.m. ET, according to the [Senate floor log](https://www.dailypress.senate.gov/thursday-november-19-2026/).

The bill now goes to the House. It is not law until the House passes it and the president signs it.

**What the bill would do**

Under the Senate-passed text, a registered exchange could not list or clear a contract that "expressly references" terrorism, assassination, war or U.S. military operations, [RG reported](https://rg.org/news/prediction-markets/senate-passes-death-bets-act-s-4035-war-death-event-contracts) from the passed version. It also could not list a contract expected to settle mainly on someone's death. The version adds U.S. military operations to the bill Sen. Adam Schiff, D-Calif., introduced in March.

A Schiff-Curtis amendment, named for Schiff and Sen. John Curtis, R-Utah, adds a rule of construction. It says the bill does not change existing law for other event contracts, including those tied to gaming, according to [DeFi Rate](https://defirate.com/news/united-states-senate-passes-amended-death-bets-act/) and RG.

**How these markets work today**

A prediction market lets people trade contracts that pay out if an event happens, such as a rate cut or an election result. In the U.S., the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) oversees such exchanges. Under the Commodity Exchange Act, the CFTC can already block war, terrorism and assassination contracts it finds contrary to the public interest, but that call is at its discretion, [Schiff's office said in March](https://www.schiff.senate.gov/news/press-releases/news-sen-schiff-introduces-legislation-to-explicitly-ban-death-and-war-prediction-contracts/). The bill would write the ban into law.

"There is no justification for gambling on lives," Schiff said in that March statement.

**What comes next**

A House companion bill, H.R. 7942, has sat in a House Agriculture subcommittee since April, DeFi Rate reported. The current Congress ends on Jan. 3, 2027. Black Mint did not find public responses to the vote from prediction market operators by 6 a.m. ET Friday.

*In our opinion: the question worth chasing is whether the House moves before Jan. 3, because a bill that stalls there starts over in the new Congress. For exchanges, the stake is a narrow but hard line in law on which contracts they can list. The CFTC would lose some of the case-by-case discretion it has today.*

articles.title: CFTC Chair Says Hyperliquid and Onchain Venues Get No Special Rules
articles.excerpt: Michael Selig said onchain derivatives venues must register as a U.S. exchange or partner with one, citing Backpack, which won three U.S. licenses this week.
articles.body_md:
CFTC Chairman Michael Selig said on Thursday, Nov. 19, that onchain venues such as Hyperliquid have two ways to serve U.S. retail traders: register as an exchange or partner with one that already is. He said they would face the same rules as traditional derivatives exchanges, with no exemption for running on a blockchain.

Selig spoke in an interview at The Hill and The Block's Capitol Crypto Forum in Washington, according to [The Block](https://www.theblock.co/news/regulation/2026-11-19-cftc-chair-selig-hyperliquid-onchain-venues-the-us-444106) and [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/11/20/cftc-tells-hyperliquid-and-crypto-rivals-no-special-rules-for-onchain-trading).

**Two doors into the U.S.**

Selig pointed to Backpack as the model for the first route. The crypto exchange gained three U.S. registrations this week: a designated contract market (an exchange), a derivatives clearing organization (a clearinghouse) and a futures commission merchant (a broker that holds customer funds), The Block reported.

The second route is a partnership with a firm that is already registered, which Selig said other platforms are pursuing, according to The Block and [TokenPost](https://www.tokenpost.com/news/regulation/61595). Hyperliquid itself is not available to U.S. customers and has no U.S. approval, [The Crypto Times](https://www.cryptotimes.io/2026/11/19/cftc-chair-outlines-regulatory-path-for-hyperliquids-us-expansion/) noted.

**How a perpetual future works**

A perpetual future is a leveraged bet on an asset's price that never expires. Instead of settling on a set date, traders on one side pay the other a small "funding" fee at regular intervals, which keeps the contract price close to the spot price. Selig said derivatives offered to U.S. retail customers must trade on a registered exchange.

**Other side of the debate**

Selig said some in crypto want lighter oversight, and that equal rules are fair to firms that already comply, according to CoinDesk and The Crypto Times. Hyperliquid did not publicly respond to the remarks in the reports Black Mint reviewed.

*In our opinion: the bigger story is the price of admission. A U.S. exchange, a clearinghouse and a broker license are not a weekend project, and Backpack just showed it can be done. For Hyperliquid, the stake is access to U.S. retail traders it cannot serve today. The first CFTC approval of a partner-based Hyperliquid product is the next filing to track.*

articles.title: VanEck Drops Gemini as Custodian of Its Bitcoin, Ether and SOL ETFs
articles.excerpt: SEC filings show Gemini's custody and clearing deals with three VanEck funds end around Feb. 16, 2027. Coinbase Custody stays on.
articles.body_md:
VanEck is ending its custody and clearing contracts with Gemini for three U.S. crypto ETFs, according to three Form 8-K filings with the SEC signed Thursday. The cutoff is on or about Feb. 16, 2027.

The funds are the VanEck Bitcoin ETF ([HODL](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1838028/000183802826000007/hodl-20261116.htm)), the VanEck Ethereum ETF ([ETHV](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1860788/000186078826000005/ethv-20261116.htm)) and the VanEck Solana ETF ([VSOL](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2028541/000202854126000014/vsol-20261116.htm)). VanEck Digital Assets, the sponsor, sent Gemini Trust Company written notice on Nov. 16, the filings say. Coinbase Custody Trust Company will keep serving as a custodian for all three.

**What a custodian does for an ETF**

A spot crypto ETF owns the actual coins. A custodian keeps those coins in secured accounts on the fund's behalf. Under these contracts, Gemini also held each fund's cash and ran a clearing service, which settles the fund's crypto trades with other Gemini customers.

For VSOL, the change reaches staking, too. Staking means locking up tokens to help run the Solana network in return for rewards. The VSOL filing says Gemini's staking addendum ends when its custody agreement does.

**Contracts that date to 2023**

The HODL agreements are dated Oct. 26, 2023, before the SEC [approved](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/gensler-statement-spot-bitcoin-011023) the first U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs on Jan. 10, 2024. The ether fund's custody deal is dated May 8, 2024, and the Solana fund's is dated June 13, 2025. Gemini will keep servicing all three funds until the cutoff.

Three months of notice. Then the handover.

The filings don't give a reason for the change. They also don't say how much of each fund's crypto Gemini holds today. [CoinDesk reported](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/11/20/vaneck-drops-gemini-as-custodian-of-its-bitcoin-ether-and-sol-etfs) that it asked VanEck and Gemini for comment on the reasons.

*In our opinion: this is a breakup served by 8-K, with a three-month notice period. Unless VanEck names a replacement, Coinbase becomes the one custodian named in these filings for all three funds, so more of their coins sit with a single provider. VSOL holders have the most open question: who runs the fund's staking after Feb. 16. Watch for a prospectus update before that date.*

articles.title: MoonPay Seeks OCC Trust Bank Charter to Issue and Hold Stablecoins
articles.excerpt: The proposed MoonPay National Trust Bank, based in Miami Beach, would take no deposits and seek no deposit insurance, its OCC application says.
articles.body_md:
MoonPay has applied to the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), the federal regulator for national banks, to open MoonPay National Trust Bank. The [application](https://www.occ.gov/topics/charters-and-licensing/digital-assets-licensing-applications/moonpay-national-trust-bank-combined-cv-pa.pdf) is dated Nov. 17, and the OCC [lists it](https://www.occ.gov/topics/charters-and-licensing/digital-assets-licensing-applications/index-digital-assets-licensing-applications.html) as received Nov. 18.

The bank would offer "fiduciary custody services," stablecoin issuance, redemption and reserve management, and "conversion services as agent," the filing says. It would be based at 407 Lincoln Road in Miami Beach, Florida. It would take no deposits, and under deposit insurance the form reads "No insurance sought."

**How a trust bank differs from a regular bank**

A national trust bank is a narrow kind of bank. It holds and manages assets for clients, but it doesn't take ordinary deposits or make loans. A stablecoin is a token meant to hold a steady value, such as one U.S. dollar. An issuer creates new tokens when clients send dollars, retires them when clients cash out, and manages the reserves that back them.

The application says the bank would serve clients through digital channels, and the Miami Beach office won't be open to the public. Key details, including the business plan, capital and financial projections, are marked confidential.

**Who would run it**

MoonPay Inc, the New York parent, would own the bank outright. Co-founder Ivan Soto-Wright would chair a five-member board and serve as interim president and CEO, the filing says. In the application, MoonPay says it has more than 30 million customers in 180 countries.

The public can comment for 30 days after a notice runs in the Miami Herald, according to the filing. MoonPay's request sits at the top of 15 pending applications on the OCC's digital-asset licensing list, which also includes Galaxy, Ramp, zerohash and Kraken parent Payward. [PANews](https://www.panews.io/articles/01a1f4af-41b0-77d8-ba24-0f5dd5f35a20) also reported the filing. The OCC has not ruled on it.

*In our opinion: this filing moves MoonPay toward the job of holding stablecoin reserves, the money that has to be there when holders cash out. A federal trust charter would put that work under OCC examiners. The detail that matters most, the bank's capital, sits in the confidential exhibits. The next marker is the close of the 30-day comment window after the Miami Herald notice.*

articles.title: Japan's Core Inflation Rises to 2.2%, Its Highest Reading of 2026
articles.excerpt: Power and gas bills drove the rise, while prices excluding energy cooled to 2.2% from 2.4%. Bitcoin was down 3.4% over 24 hours.
articles.body_md:
Japan's core consumer prices rose 2.2% in October from a year earlier, up from 2.1% in September, the [Statistics Bureau of Japan](https://www.stat.go.jp/data/cpi/sokuhou/tsuki/index-z.htm) said Friday morning Tokyo time, Thursday evening ET. That's the highest reading of 2026.

Economists polled by Reuters had expected 2.3%, [CNBC reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/20/japan-inflation-cpi-october.html). Headline inflation rose to 2.3% from 2.1%.

**Energy did the lifting**

Energy prices rose 2.2% from a year earlier after falling 0.6% in September, the [bureau's report](https://www.stat.go.jp/data/cpi/sokuhou/tsuki/pdf/zenkoku.pdf) shows. Electricity went from a 2.4% drop to a 1.6% gain, and city gas rose 5.3% after 0.2%. Household energy subsidies expired in September, CNBC said.

Strip out energy and the picture cooled. Prices excluding fresh food and energy rose 2.2%, down from 2.4%. Rice other than the Koshihikari variety fell 29.8%.

**How Japan measures inflation**

The consumer price index tracks what a set basket of goods and services costs each month. Japan's "core" measure leaves out fresh food, because weather swings those prices around. The Bank of Japan aims for 2% inflation. A year ago, core inflation ran at 3.0%; it fell to 1.4% in April and May before climbing back.

**Market reaction**

The Nikkei 225 fell 2.1% after the data, and the yen traded at 159.59 per dollar, CNBC reported. LSEG data put the odds of a quarter-point BOJ hike in December at 72%, per CNBC. Higher Japanese rates raise the cost of borrowing in yen.

Bitcoin traded at $61,410 at 11:54 p.m. ET Thursday, down 3.4% over 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion: the headline rose, but the measure without energy slowed, so October's increase came mostly from power and gas bills. That hands the BOJ a mixed read heading into December. Households carry the near-term cost; yen borrowers carry the rate risk if the hike comes. Tokyo's November CPI on Nov. 27 is the next data point.*

articles.title: Sky's USDS Supply Falls 38% After Report on Illicit-Linked Swaps
articles.excerpt: About $2 billion of USDS left circulation in a day as the token held near $1. Sky said its peg reserve is working as designed.
articles.body_md:
The supply of Sky's USDS stablecoin fell about 38% in one day, to $3.24 billion at 5:47 p.m. ET Thursday from $5.24 billion a day earlier, [DefiLlama data show](https://defillama.com/stablecoin/sky-dollar). The token held its peg, trading at $1.00 on [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/usds).

The exits followed a [CoinDesk report](https://www.coindesk.com/business/2026/11/19/north-korean-hackers-used-sky-s-stablecoin-system-putting-billions-at-freeze-risk) Thursday morning on research by risk firm Inca Digital. Inca traced $518 million in transactions through Sky's Peg Stability Module that involved wallets it linked to hackers, sanctioned entities and other illicit actors. Inca tied about $101.9 million of that to North Korean actors, including wallets funded from the February 2025 Bybit hack, according to the report.

**How the reserve works**

The Peg Stability Module, or PSM, is a pool that lets anyone swap Circle's USDC for Sky's USDS or DAI at about one to one. When USDS slips below $1, traders can turn it in for USDC, which pulls the price back up. Circle can freeze USDC; USDS has no such switch. Inca's concern, as CoinDesk reported it, is that the USDC sits in one shared address. A court-ordered freeze could lock the whole pool along with the flagged money.

**One holder drove most of the exits**

More than $1.5 billion in USDC left the PSM after the report, most of it from one large holder whose address is attributed to the Poloniex exchange, [CoinDesk reported](https://www.coindesk.com/business/2026/11/19/sky-s-usds-stablecoin-shrinks-35-as-usd1-5-billion-exits-reserves-after-illicit-finance-report), citing blockchain data. The report noted the label doesn't show who started the trades.

**Sky's response**

Sky [said on X](https://x.com/SkyEcosystem/status/2123466923371282791) that the PSM has processed more than $968 billion since launch, so the alleged figures equal about 0.03% of volume. It said the activity ran mostly through third-party platforms, and its own front ends block flagged wallets.

Rune Christensen, founder of Sky, formerly MakerDAO, [wrote](https://x.com/RuneKek/status/2123500695802253539) that USDS is backed by about $10 billion in collateral and that Sky "handled over $2B in outflows in the past day." He said peg liquidity "never dropped below $2B." He added that Sky's Core Council announced a 5.25 million USDS buyback of SKY tokens over seven days.

*In our opinion: the peg held on Thursday while about $2 billion left. The harder question is legal. If a court or police agency ever asks Circle to freeze the pooled USDC, every holder who relies on that pool would share the hit along with the flagged wallets. The next thing to watch is whether Sky adds wallet screening at the protocol level.*

articles.title: Anthropic Closes Day One at $97.17, 17% Above Its $83 IPO Price
articles.excerpt: The Claude maker opened at $111.50 before giving back part of the gain. Its $81.3 billion offering is the largest IPO on record.
articles.body_md:
Anthropic shares closed at $97.17 in their Nasdaq debut Thursday, 17% above the $83 offer price, after opening at $111.50, [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/19/anthropic-ipo-ant-live-updates.html) and [AP](https://apnews.com/article/anthropic-ipo-nasdaq-ai-b6a74b8949021207dc162fcc876c4649) reported.

The AI company, which trades under the ticker ANT, raised $81.3 billion by selling 980 million shares. That tops SpaceX's record of about $75 billion from June, [AP said](https://apnews.com/article/anthropic-ipo-by-numbers-fdca56f1cda70c9908899057e7e591e6).

**A $14 Slide From the Open**

At the opening price, the company was valued at about $2.01 trillion, according to AP. By the close, its fully diluted market value was roughly $1.8 trillion, CNBC reported. That ranks it behind only Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia, Alphabet, Amazon and SpaceX among U.S. companies, per CNBC.

More than 846 million shares changed hands, CNBC said, compared with 522 million on SpaceX's first day.

**How an IPO price and an opening price differ**

The $83 price was set Wednesday night by the company and its banks. Only investors who got an allocation, mostly institutions, paid it. The opening price comes later, from an auction on the exchange that matches all the buy and sell orders waiting for the first trade.

So the gap matters. Shares bought at $83 closed up about 17%. Shares bought at the $111.50 open closed down about 13%, by our math.

**Why crypto traders noticed**

Bitcoin was little changed on the day. It traded near $62,196 at 5:47 p.m. ET, down about 0.3% over 24 hours, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

The deal also reached the Federal Reserve's debate. Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said on a call with reporters that what early holders do with their new access to cash "is going to become a macro-relevant statistic," [Reuters reported](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/feds-goolsbee-says-ai-surge-could-strain-us-capacity-overheat-economy-5039887). More money spent can mean more pressure on prices, and that feeds into rate decisions.

*In our opinion: the first day handed out two very different report cards, depending on what time investors showed up. The bigger number is the paper wealth now sitting with early holders, which the Fed says it is watching. The next dates that matter are the lockup expiries, when insiders can first sell, and the Fed's Dec. 8-9 meeting.*

articles.title: Fed's Goolsbee Says AI Boom Risks Overheating the U.S. Economy
articles.excerpt: The Chicago Fed chief called inflation 'borderline, disturbingly high' and said all options are on the table before the Dec. 8-9 meeting.
articles.body_md:
Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said Thursday the AI investment boom is adding to the risk of the U.S. economy overheating, and he said all options are on the table for the Fed's December meeting, [Reuters reported](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/feds-goolsbee-says-ai-surge-could-strain-us-capacity-overheat-economy-5039887).

"The AI boom is contributing to the potential of overheating in the economy," Goolsbee said on a call with reporters, according to Reuters. He described inflation as "borderline, disturbingly high," a phrase [Bloomberg Law](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/capital-markets/feds-goolsbee-says-all-options-on-fomc-table-amid-hot-inflation) also reported.

**December Hike Size Left Open**

The Fed's benchmark rate sits at 3.75% to 4% after its October meeting, [per the Fed's minutes](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomcminutes20261028.htm). Markets widely expect a quarter-point hike at the Dec. 8-9 meeting, Reuters said. Goolsbee didn't say whether he would back a larger half-point move, which at least one colleague has called for. Bloomberg Law reported he did not push back on that possibility.

"The evidence does not suggest we're on a path back to 2%," he said, per Reuters.

**What overheating means**

An economy overheats when spending runs ahead of what it can produce. Workers, power and chips get scarce, and prices rise. Goolsbee pointed to data-center building and to people spending out of new stock wealth. A rate hike raises borrowing costs, which slows that spending.

He also flagged Anthropic's record IPO. "The question of what people are going to do with the money now that they have some access to that liquidity is going to become a macro-relevant statistic," he said, per Reuters.

**The other side of the AI story**

Goolsbee said at an earlier Indiana event that AI may still bring a productivity boom, [Reuters reported](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/goolsbee-says-feds-job-now-182859763.html). He said it isn't yet clear what AI will do to the economy's capacity, noting that past general-purpose technologies took years to spread.

**Where crypto fits**

Higher rates lift the return on cash and Treasury bills. Bitcoin pays no interest, so it competes with those yields. Bitcoin traded near $62,196 at 5:47 p.m. ET, down about 0.3% over 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion: the part worth noting is the link Goolsbee drew. He tied the AI build-out and a single stock listing directly to the Fed's inflation fight. That turns Wall Street's AI wealth into a rate-policy question as well as a stock-market story. The next marker is the size of the Dec. 9 decision: a quarter point, as markets expect, or the half point some officials want.*

articles.title: SEC Says Eight Firms Ran Fake Crypto Platforms, Taking $37 Million
articles.excerpt: The SEC complaint says social media ads led investors into group chats, then to fake trading sites backed by forged SEC certificates.
articles.body_md:
The Securities and Exchange Commission on Thursday charged eight Colorado-based entities with taking more than $37 million from U.S. investors through fake crypto trading platforms, [the agency said](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2026-115-sec-eight-entities-used-fake-crypto-asset-trading-platforms-steal-more-37-million-us-investors). The SEC said the people running them were likely overseas.

These are allegations in a civil complaint filed in federal court in Colorado, and none has been proven. The SEC's announcement included no response from the defendants.

**How the SEC says the scheme worked**

According to the complaint, social media ads steered investors into group and private chats. People in those chats posed as staff of an investment adviser. They first gave tips on trading U.S. stocks, the SEC said, then pushed victims to send as much money as possible to a supposed crypto trading platform.

The SEC said the adviser and the exchange were both fake, even as investors were led to believe they were buying real crypto. To look legitimate, the operators allegedly made fake SEC certificates and filed paperwork with the SEC, FINRA and FinCEN. Then they pointed doubtful investors to those filings.

Filing a form with a regulator isn't the same as being approved by one. A filing on its own doesn't mean the agency vetted the business.

**Four pairs, swapped every few months**

The scheme ran from August 2024 through May 2026 as four adviser-and-exchange pairs, the agency said. Each pair ran for a few months before the operators moved on to the next one.

The eight defendants are Advisor WeChat Capital, Tech Brokerage Asset Alliance Ltd., HB Wealth Advisors, IdeaCrypto Exchange LLC, Convergent Wealth Advisors Inc., RealSimple Crypto Exchange Inc., Associated Wealth Advisors Ltd. and Essential Crypto Exchange. The SEC alleges fraud under the Securities Exchange Act, plus Investment Advisers Act violations for some. It wants injunctions, repayment with interest, and civil penalties.

"The SEC continues to seek out and expose fraudulent investment scams that prey on U.S. investors," said Laura D'Allaird, who leads the SEC's Cyber and Emerging Technologies Unit. Regulators in Hong Kong, Singapore, China and Switzerland helped with the case, the SEC said.

*In our opinion: the detail worth noting is the fake paperwork. These operators allegedly used real regulators' names to win trust, and kept changing brands every few months. The SEC says investors can check anyone selling an investment on Investor.gov. If the operators really are overseas, getting the $37 million back will be the hard part.*

articles.title: IOSCO Warns Blockchains Face a Harder Road to Quantum-Safe Crypto
articles.excerpt: Post-quantum signatures are about 35 to 40 times bigger, the global securities body said. A Solana test saw throughput fall about 90%.
articles.body_md:
The International Organization of Securities Commissions told financial firms on Thursday to start preparing for quantum computers now, and said blockchains face a harder switch than most. Its [63-page final report](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD833.pdf) cites conservative estimates that machines able to break today's encryption could arrive between 2030 and 2035.

IOSCO's members regulate more than 99% of the world's financial markets, [the group says](https://www.iosco.org/news/pdf/IOSCONEWS810.pdf).

**Why blockchains have the heavier lift**

Ethereum, Solana and Tron sign transactions with elliptic curve cryptography, or ECC. Each ECC signature takes about 64 bytes. A large enough quantum machine would be able to work out the private key, the secret that controls the coins, from a public key the network can see.

The fix is a quantum-resistant signature, and those are bulky. One U.S. standard, ML-DSA-44, makes signatures of about 2,420 bytes, roughly 35 to 40 times larger, the report said. Bigger signatures fill blocks faster. IOSCO cited a quantum-resistant Solana testnet where throughput fell about 90%.

A bank can patch its systems overnight. A blockchain can't. Changing its signature rules takes a hard fork, an upgrade every node must adopt, and no one can force validators to move at once. Coins at old addresses stay exposed until their owners move them, and dormant coins with missing owners may never move.

**Some firms are waiting on regulators**

Several industry participants told IOSCO to plan for the possibility that such machines arrive within five years, sped up by AI. Even so, most firms are still at the awareness and planning stage. Some survey answers described "quantum-procrastination," which means waiting on regulators before acting.

"Practical quantum computers capable of compromising widely used cryptography do not yet exist, but the scale and duration of the transition mean the financial sector should start preparing today," IOSCO Board Chair Jean-Paul Servais said. The group also told regulators to act against "quantum washing," where firms overstate their quantum work. It named quantum a priority for 2027. [Decrypt](https://decrypt.co/383613/quantum-upgrade-could-be-particularly-challenging-for-blockchains-iosco) also reported the findings.

*In our opinion: the number to remember is 90%. That is how much throughput one test network gave up for quantum safety, and it shows the trade every chain will have to price in. The firms waiting for regulators now have their answer from the regulators' own club. The next markers are IOSCO's 2027 work and whether the big chains set fork dates.*

articles.title: Bitcoin ETFs Shed $306.5 Million, Taking November Outflows to $2.89B
articles.excerpt: Outflows hit 11 of 13 trading days this month, Farside data show. BlackRock's IBIT led Wednesday's exits as bitcoin traded near $63,100.
articles.body_md:
Investors pulled $306.5 million out of U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs on Wednesday, [Farside Investors data show](https://farside.co.uk/btc/). That brings November's net outflows to about $2.89 billion across 13 trading days.

Only two days this month ended with money coming in: $74.6 million on Nov. 4 and $7.9 million on Monday. The other 11 were outflow days.

**IBIT led Wednesday's exits**

- BlackRock's IBIT: -$148.7 million
- Fidelity's FBTC: -$69.3 million
- Bitwise's BITB: -$36.6 million
- Grayscale's GBTC: -$20.3 million
- ARK's ARKB: -$19.3 million

No fund posted an inflow on the day. The two worst days of the month were Nov. 5, at -$430.2 million, and Nov. 6, at -$411.9 million.

**How ETF flows work**

A spot bitcoin ETF holds actual bitcoin for its shareholders. When investors sell more shares than they buy, large brokers called authorized participants hand shares back to the fund. The fund then delivers or sells bitcoin to cover them. A net outflow means the fund's bitcoin holdings shrink, and an inflow means it buys more. The flow number tracks demand from people who hold bitcoin through a brokerage account.

**Price held up on Thursday**

Bitcoin traded near $63,100 at 11:50 a.m. ET Thursday, up about 1% over 24 hours, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin). Ether was near $1,779, up about 2.3%. [Decrypt](https://decrypt.co/383597/bitcoin-struggles-to-hold-64000-as-etf-outflows-hit-2-9b-in-november) also reported the month's outflows near $2.9 billion. Farside had not yet posted Thursday's figures.

Even after this month, the funds still hold about $54.2 billion in net inflows since they launched in January 2024, by Farside's count. IBIT alone accounts for about $63.9 billion, while GBTC is about $28.2 billion in the red.

*In our opinion: the bigger story is the streak. November's average is about $220 million out per session, and no single day topped $431 million. Even so, $2.89 billion is real money walking out the door. The number that matters next is whether the last seven trading days of November, Thanksgiving week included, can pull that total back toward zero.*

articles.title: Singapore Sells S$100 Million of Tokenized Bills Settled in CBDC
articles.excerpt: Five banks bid more than twice the amount on offer. MAS will rename its test network SG Digital Ledger and expand the trials in 2027.
articles.body_md:
Singapore's central bank sold S$100 million (about $77 million) of four-week bills as blockchain tokens and settled the sale in wholesale central bank digital currency, the [Monetary Authority of Singapore said on Thursday](https://www.mas.gov.sg/news/media-releases/2026/mas-announces-successful-issuance-of-tokenised-mas-bills-on-the-singapore-dollar-test-network).

The bills were issued on Nov. 6 and mature on Dec. 4. Bids came to more than double the size of the sale, MAS said.

**Five Banks Took Part**

The bidders were MAS's five primary dealers, the banks approved to make markets in Singapore government and MAS securities: DBS, HSBC's Singapore branch, OCBC, Standard Chartered and UOB. The auction used a uniform price, with a minimum denomination of S$1,000, according to [MAS's issue page](https://www.mas.gov.sg/bonds-and-bills/auctions-and-issuance-calendar/mas-bills-type-tokenised-mas-bill). [The Block](https://www.theblock.co/news/web3/2026-11-19-singapores-mas-tokenized-bills-443562) and [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/business/2026/11/19/singapore-settles-usd77-5-million-tokenized-bill-sale-in-local-cbdc) also reported the sale.

Managing Director Chia Der Jiun said the sale "allowed us to test a new method of issuance." He added that tokenized bills "can play a complementary role to conventional MAS Bills" over time.

**How a Native Token Bill Works**

Most tokenized assets start as a normal security, and a token is created later to represent it. That means two records that have to be matched. MAS issued these bills directly on its own ledger, so the token is the bill. Buyers paid in wholesale CBDC, a digital form of central bank money that only financial institutions can hold. Because cash and bills sit on the same network, both sides of the trade can settle together.

The bills matter because banks can pledge them as collateral. In 2025, banks used the same network for an overnight interbank loan settled in wholesale CBDC. Tokenized bills give those loans a trusted asset to borrow against.

**Network Gets a New Name**

In a [keynote at the Singapore FinTech Festival](https://www.mas.gov.sg/news/speeches/2026/keynote-address-by-md-at-the-singapore-fintech-festival-2026), Chia said the Singapore Dollar Test Network will become an operational service called SG Digital Ledger. He also said MAS views crypto assets as unsuitable for retail investors, while tokenized financial assets have benefits for wholesale markets. MAS plans bigger issues and more participants in live trials in 2027.

*In our opinion: S$100 million is small for a central bank. The part that matters is the plumbing. The banks that move collateral all day now have a government-backed token they can pledge. The number to watch is how big the 2027 issues get, and whether MAS adds foreign government bonds and money market funds, as Chia said it could.*

articles.title: Kraken Parent Payward to Buy Tribe Capital, a $2.7 Billion VC Firm
articles.excerpt: Kraken co-CEO Arjun Sethi co-founded and chairs Tribe. The deal price wasn't disclosed, and closing is expected in the first quarter of 2027.
articles.body_md:
Payward, the company that owns crypto exchange Kraken, agreed to buy venture firm Tribe Capital Management, which manages $2.7 billion, the companies [said on Wednesday](https://www.payward.com/press-release/payward-to-acquire-tribe-capital). Financial terms were not disclosed.

The deal is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, subject to customary conditions, including required consents. Tribe will sit inside Payward's asset management arm, next to its trading, banking, services and AI businesses.

**What Payward Says It Gets**

Payward said customers want access to early-stage companies and private-market deals. Tribe brings the work of finding, vetting and running those investments. Payward plans to pair that with its custody, trading, collateral and tokenization systems to build new private-market products, the [release on Business Wire](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261118447119/en/Payward-to-Acquire-Tribe-Capital-Adding-Private-Market-Capabilities-to-Its-Platform) said.

"We see a strong fit between our investment approach and Payward's infrastructure, distribution, and product-building capabilities," Tribe co-founder Jonathan Hsu said in the release.

Tribe was founded in 2018 and invests in early- and late-stage private companies through pooled funds and co-investment vehicles, which let backers put money into a single deal alongside a fund.

**The Leadership Overlap**

Arjun Sethi, Kraken's co-CEO, co-founded Tribe and chairs it, [The Block](https://www.theblock.co/news/business/2026-11-18-kraken-parent-payward-tribe-capital-443522) and [Unchained](https://unchainedcrypto.com/krakens-owner-payward-strikes-deal-for-tribe-capital-a-2-7-billion-venture-investor/) reported. Unchained noted that the announcement does not describe what part, if any, Sethi played in negotiating or approving the deal. Payward has not said publicly how the deal was reviewed internally.

**Why Tokenization Comes Up**

Tokenization means issuing a share or fund stake as a blockchain token so it can be held and traded on crypto rails. Kraken already offers tokenized stocks through its xStocks business, which Unchained reported now lists more than 1,500 assets. Private-company shares are harder to buy and sell than listed stocks, which is the gap Payward says it wants to fill.

*In our opinion: The bigger story is that a crypto exchange is buying its way into venture capital and private deals. The open question is governance, since the buyer's co-CEO chairs the firm being bought, and the price is not public. We'll be watching for deal terms and any filing ahead of the first-quarter close.*

articles.title: Hong Kong SFC Adds Hyperliquid to Its Unlicensed Platform Alert List
articles.excerpt: The regulator says Hyperliquid's trading site isn't SFC-licensed and is suspected of serving Hong Kong users. The listing carries no fine or court finding.
articles.body_md:
Hong Kong's Securities and Futures Commission added "Hyperliquid / Hyperliquid Hong Kong" to its alert list of suspicious virtual asset trading platforms on Nov. 18, [according to the regulator's entry](https://www.sfc.hk/en/alert-list/3963). It names the website app.hyperliquid.xyz/trade.

The SFC said the entity is not licensed by it and is "suspected of operating, or holding itself out as operating, a virtual asset trading platform in Hong Kong and/or actively marketing its services to the Hong Kong public."

**What the Alert List Is**

The list is a public warning, not a fine, a court ruling or a block on the site. The SFC uses it to flag platforms that appear to serve Hong Kong residents without a license. Its standard notice says users of an unlicensed platform are not protected by SFC supervision and may lose everything if the platform fails or is hacked. Hyperliquid is the newest name on the list, which also includes BTCC, added on Oct. 22, per the [SFC alert list](https://www.sfc.hk/en/alert_list).

[Crypto Briefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/hong-kong-sfc-flags-hyperliquid/) and [The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/regulation/hong-kong-sfc-adds-hyperliquid-to-platform-alert-list) also reported the listing.

**How Hyperliquid Works**

Hyperliquid runs its own blockchain, and its core includes on-chain order books for perpetual futures and spot trading, [according to its documentation](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs). Perpetual futures are derivatives that let traders bet on a price with borrowed money and no expiry date. Users keep control of their own funds instead of depositing them with a company, Crypto Briefing reported.

That design is why the case is worth following. Hong Kong licenses platforms based on who they serve, and the SFC's entry does not say how it treats an exchange that runs on a blockchain with no local firm behind it.

**No Response Yet**

Hyperliquid's official X account had not posted about the listing as of 5:50 a.m. ET on Thursday. The SFC entry lists no address or operating company.

*In our opinion: The question worth chasing is who answers for a platform that has no Hong Kong office. The listing is a warning to Hong Kong users about the risk, and the SFC has not announced any block on the site. The next step to watch is whether Hyperliquid responds or limits access from Hong Kong.*

articles.title: Anthropic Prices Record IPO at $83 a Share, Raising $81.3 Billion
articles.excerpt: The Claude maker sold 980 million shares above its $70-$78 range, valuing it near $1.5 trillion. Trading on Nasdaq as ANT is set for Thursday.
articles.body_md:
Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 a share on Wednesday, raising about $81.3 billion in the largest IPO on record, the company and [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/18/anthropic-ipo-ai-offering-price.html) said.

The shares are expected to start trading Thursday on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker "ANT," and the offering is expected to close on Nov. 20, according to [Anthropic's statement](https://www.anthropic.com/news/anthropic-prices-initial-public-offering).

**Priced Above the Range**

The company had marketed the shares at $70 to $78 and planned to sell 825 million, CNBC and [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/18/anthropic-reportedly-prices-ipo-at-83-a-share-above-projected-range/) reported. It instead sold 980 million. Of those, 956,351,354 came from Anthropic and 23,648,646 from selling stockholders and Anthropic receives no money from their sales.

At $83, Anthropic is valued at about $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis, [AP](https://apnews.com/article/anthropic-ipo-pricing-70b660ddf900d90bbf484ecdf1fb441c) and CNBC reported. The previous record belonged to SpaceX, which raised $75 billion in its June IPO before underwriters bought extra shares, CNBC and TechCrunch said.

**How IPO Pricing Works**

Banks running an IPO collect orders from big investors before the listing, then set one price for everyone. Pricing above the marketed range means demand ran ahead of supply. Underwriters here also hold a 30-day option to buy up to 147 million more shares, a tool used to steady trading in the first weeks.

**The Crypto Backdrop**

The deal lands in a weak week for digital assets. Bitcoin traded at $63,487 at 11:47 p.m. ET Wednesday, down 1.3% in 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin). U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs had net outflows of $157.8 million on Nov. 18, according to [Farside Investors](https://farside.co.uk/btc/).

Anthropic reported $33.24 billion in revenue for the nine months through Sept. 30 and a $104 billion net loss, mostly from fair-value changes on convertible notes and derivatives, CNBC reported from the prospectus.

*In our opinion: An $81 billion check is a lot of risk appetite pointed at one ticker, in the same week bitcoin funds saw money leave. It shows where big investors are placing bets right now. Thursday's first trade on Nasdaq is the number to watch, and the underwriters' 147 million-share option will show whether demand holds past day one.*

articles.title: Six Senators Ask Treasury for Safe Harbor for State Stablecoin Issuers
articles.excerpt: Lummis, Gillibrand and four others say Treasury's GENIUS Act proposal shields issuers awaiting federal approval but not those under state rules.
articles.body_md:
A bipartisan group of six senators asked Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Wednesday to give state-regulated stablecoin issuers the same temporary protection his department has proposed for issuers awaiting federal approval, [according to Sen. Cynthia Lummis's office](https://pubt.io/view/6B715824E707EAFF9C806441041BE434AB046C0C).

Republicans Lummis of Wyoming, Kevin Cramer of North Dakota and Pete Ricketts of Nebraska signed the letter with Democrats Kirsten Gillibrand of New York, Angela Alsobrooks of Maryland and Mark Warner of Virginia, [The Block reported](https://www.theblock.co/news/regulation/2026-11-18-senators-treasury-must-ensure-equal-footing-for-stablecoin-issuers-in-genius-act-implementation-443501).

**What the Senators Want Changed**

The GENIUS Act, the federal stablecoin law, lets issuers with $10 billion or less in outstanding stablecoins operate under a state regime if that regime is "substantially similar" to the federal one. Treasury's proposed rule offers a safe harbor to issuers with pending applications at federal regulators, if the regulator grants a waiver, but has no matching protection for state issuers, the senators wrote.

They asked Treasury to cover issuers in states that have certified their rules while a federal review committee examines those certifications in 2027. "For Treasury to finalize this proposal in a way that reflects Congressional intent, it must allow issuers to choose from state or federal charters, as contemplated by the GENIUS Act, without the risk of business disruption or uncertainty," the senators wrote.

**What a Safe Harbor Does**

A stablecoin is a crypto token designed to track a currency such as the U.S. dollar and backed by reserve assets. A safe harbor lets a company keep operating under the old setup while regulators finish their review. Without one, a state-licensed issuer could face a gap in which it is unsure whether it may keep issuing new tokens.

Lummis's office said the law already gives Wyoming, New York and Nebraska an expedited certification path. Four of the senators wrote to Bessent on the same issue in June, The Block reported. A public response from Treasury to the new letter could not be found as of early Thursday.

*In our opinion: The fight is over who supervises the smaller issuers, and the letter carries signatures from both parties. State-chartered firms in Wyoming and New York carry the risk if the rule is finalized as written. The final Treasury rule is the document to watch, since it decides whether a state charter keeps working during the 2027 review.*

articles.title: Hyperscale Data Flags Going-Concern Doubt Over $74.8M AI Build
articles.excerpt: The former bitcoin miner had $17.3 million in cash against $231.2 million in current liabilities on Sept. 30, its new quarterly filing shows.
articles.body_md:
Hyperscale Data (GPUS), a former bitcoin miner turning its Michigan site into an AI data center, said in a [quarterly filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/896493/000121465926014565/hd111226110q.htm) on Wednesday that it still needs about $74.8 million to finish the build, and that there is "substantial doubt" about its ability to continue as a going concern.

**The Cash Gap**

As of Sept. 30, the company had about $17.3 million in cash and cash equivalents and $27.8 million in restricted cash, against $231.2 million in current liabilities, the 10-Q shows. Current liabilities exceeded current assets by about $128.1 million. It reported a net loss of about $62.1 million for the first nine months of 2026. [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/11/19/bitcoin-miner-that-sold-its-last-btc-warns-it-may-run-short-of-cash-for-usd1-2-billion-ai-deal) reported the same figures.

The project in Dowagiac, Michigan, is set to deliver about 20 megawatts of power capacity to an AI infrastructure customer. Hyperscale estimates the total cost at $122.1 million, with $47.3 million paid through Oct. 31. It expects to spend about $27.4 million in November and December and $47.4 million in the first quarter of 2027.

**What a Going-Concern Warning Means**

Auditing rules require management to say when it cannot show it has enough money to pay its bills for the next 12 months. The warning does not mean a company is shutting down. It means survival depends on raising money or selling assets. Hyperscale said it plans to use equity sales, debt, asset sales or other deals, but that those steps are not fully in its control.

**Bitcoin Sold, Contract Terms**

On Nov. 6 the company sold about 211.6 bitcoin for about $16 million and used part of the money to repay convertible notes, the filing says. CoinDesk reported that sale emptied its bitcoin holdings.

Hyperscale has cited a contract value of about $1.2 billion. The filing says that figure assumes the customer exercises two five-year extensions and that Hyperscale meets its obligations under the agreement.

*In our opinion: The headline contract number is $1.2 billion, but the figure that decides this story is $74.8 million, due over the next few months. Miners moving into AI trade a volatile coin for big construction bills, and shareholders carry the funding risk in between. Watch for new financing filings before the first phase is due to go live.*

articles.title: Fed Minutes Show Almost All Officials Expect More Rate Hikes
articles.excerpt: The October minutes show a 10-2 vote to hold at 3.75%-4%, two dissents for a hike, and wide concern that AI spending is feeding inflation.
articles.body_md:
Almost all Federal Reserve officials judged at their Oct. 27-28 meeting that further interest rate increases "would likely be appropriate," according to [minutes released Wednesday](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomcminutes20261028.htm). The committee still held its benchmark rate at 3.75% to 4% in a 10-2 vote.

Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented, preferring a quarter-point hike at that meeting, the minutes show. A couple of officials said an increase of more than 25 basis points, or a quarter of a percentage point, could warrant consideration at the next meeting if inflation data came in unfavorable.

**How Fed Minutes Work**

The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), the Fed group that sets short-term rates, publishes minutes three weeks after each decision. They summarize the debate without naming speakers. They count heads in words, from "a couple" up to "almost all." Officials who backed the October hold pointed to the benefit of gathering more information first, the minutes said.

**AI Spending Enters the Inflation Debate**

"Many participants viewed the AI buildout as a material source of inflation risk," the minutes said. The worry is that the data-center boom raises demand faster than capacity can expand. Officials also looked at the debt behind it: most said AI-related debt "had grown rapidly," much of it through "complex and opaque financing structures." Several noted the staff view that the financial system remained resilient and banks were well capitalized.

**From Rates to Crypto**

A rate hike raises what savers earn on cash and Treasury bills. That raises the bar for assets that pay no interest, such as bitcoin. Bitcoin traded at $62,196 at 5:55 p.m. ET, down 3.9% over 24 hours, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

Futures markets fully price a quarter-point hike at the Dec. 8-9 meeting, [CNBC reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/18/fed-minutes-october-2026.html), citing CME Group's FedWatch tool.

*In our opinion: The October hold read as patient on the day, but the minutes show a committee with its coat already on, waiting for one more look at the data. The new wrinkle is AI: the Fed now treats the data-center boom as both an inflation source and a debt risk, which ties the rate story crypto traders follow to tech balance sheets. The date to circle is Dec. 9, and the detail to watch is whether more than "a couple" of officials back a half-point move.*

articles.title: Abu Dhabi Court Grants Binance $6.5 Billion Freezing Order After Hack
articles.excerpt: Circle, World Liberty Financial and 16 other firms must keep stolen tokens frozen, court papers show. Tether is not covered. A hearing is set for Dec. 1.
articles.body_md:
Binance said Wednesday it obtained a $6.5 billion worldwide freezing order from the Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) Courts against the unidentified attackers behind its Oct. 29 hack, [The Block](https://www.theblock.co/news/business/2026-11-18-binance-freezing-court-order-adgm-crypto-october-hack-443491) and [Reuters](https://live.euronext.com/en/financial-news/uae-court-orders-freeze-crypto-tokens-stolen-binance-wallets) reported.

The $6.5 billion is the maximum value the order covers. Binance has said about $2.85 billion of the roughly $6.34 billion in assets hit by the hack was frozen or intercepted by third parties. U.S. authorities have attributed the attack to North Korea, Reuters reported.

**Who the Order Covers**

Circle, World Liberty Financial and 16 other companies must keep tokens tied to the hack frozen pending further proceedings, according to court documents seen by Reuters. They also may not lend, swap or mix those tokens with other assets. The court said the 18 firms are not accused of wrongdoing.

Tether, which has said it froze $1.5 billion in USDT, was not named in the order. "In consultation with the relevant authorities, we will work directly with Binance in respect of reissuing the tokens," a Tether spokesperson said, according to Reuters.

**How a Freezing Order Works on a Blockchain**

A freezing order bars the people it targets from moving assets up to a set value. Stablecoin issuers such as Circle and Tether can lock tokens in their own contracts. Binance said some issuers and exchanges require a court order before they release frozen funds.

Binance's lawyers at Gibson Dunn said the orders can be served via the blockchain. They also said a "living list" of 26,000 wallet addresses holding stolen assets will be updated as the funds move, [The Block reported](https://www.theblock.co/news/business/2026-11-18-binance-freezing-court-order-adgm-crypto-october-hack-443491).

**Responses**

Binance said in a blog post that it had absorbed the loss and made customers whole, Reuters reported. A World Liberty Financial spokesman said the company "acted decisively to protect our users and our partners." Circle did not immediately respond to Reuters.

A further hearing is set for Dec. 1, when the court will consider whether the asset-specific freeze should continue and on what terms.

*In our opinion: The figure to track is the $2.85 billion that third parties have already frozen, since the $6.5 billion is a legal ceiling. A court order gives cautious issuers the paperwork they asked for, and that is the practical gain here. The Dec. 1 hearing will show whether the freeze holds, and whether Tether's separate route returns funds faster.*

articles.title: Variational Raises $110 Million at $1.5 Billion Valuation, Led by Bain
articles.excerpt: The on-chain derivatives platform says its Omni app has handled $475 billion in volume since early 2025, with more than half now in stocks and commodities.
articles.body_md:
Variational, an on-chain derivatives platform, said Wednesday it raised $110 million in a Series B round led by Bain Capital Crypto at a $1.5 billion valuation, according to a [company release](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261116481769/en/Variational-Raises-%24110M-Series-B-at-%241.5B-Valuation-To-Scale-On-Chain-Access-To-Global-Markets). Dragonfly, HSG and Peak XV also took part, [Reuters reported](https://live.euronext.com/en/financial-news/variational-valued-15-billion-bain-led-funding-round).

The round more than doubles the $50 million Series A that Dragonfly led in [May](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260520402312/en/Variational-Secures-%2450M-to-Bring-Liquidity-from-Traditional-Markets-To-Crypto).

**What Omni Does**

Variational runs Omni, a trading platform offering leveraged bets on more than 550 crypto and traditional markets, including stocks, indexes, commodities and currencies. A derivative is a contract whose value tracks another asset, so a trader can bet on gold or an index without owning it.

Omni charges no trading fees. Instead, an in-house liquidity provider quotes every price and earns the spread (the gap between the buy and sell price), the company said. That provider pulls prices from crypto exchanges and traditional firms, including what Variational called "a tier-1 market maker."

**The Traction Numbers**

Since launching in early 2025, Omni has processed more than $475 billion in volume and holds more than $1.3 billion in open interest, the value of all open positions, the company said. Reuters carried the same figures. Variational said more than half of daily volume is now in traditional markets, and that it has more than 100,000 accounts.

The company said the money will lift open-interest caps that traders keep hitting and add hundreds of new markets, with 24/7 swaps trading and a trading API planned.

**Open Questions**

All traction figures come from Variational and have not been independently audited. The release does not say which countries can use Omni or how its stock and commodity contracts are regulated. Leveraged trading can multiply losses as well as gains.

*In our opinion: The company is betting that traders want stock and oil exposure on crypto rails, and the volume split suggests some already do. The risk sits with the in-house liquidity provider on the other side of every trade, so how it is capitalized matters more than the valuation. Watch whether Variational publishes audited figures and says where Omni is licensed.*

articles.title: Visa Brings Stablecoin Funding for Visa Direct Payouts to Asia-Pacific
articles.excerpt: Singapore's dtcpay is the first pilot partner. Businesses fund payouts with stablecoins while recipients get local currency, Visa said.
articles.body_md:
Visa said Wednesday it plans to let eligible clients in Asia-Pacific fund cross-border payouts on its Visa Direct network, which it says reaches more than 18 billion endpoints, with stablecoins, according to a [Visa press release](https://www.visa.com.sg/about-visa/newsroom/press-releases/visa-direct-advances-stablecoin-powered-money-movement-in-asia-pacific.html).

Singapore payments firm dtcpay is the first pilot partner. The people getting paid won't touch crypto: recipients still receive local currency, Visa said.

**What Prefunding Means**

Visa Direct is Visa's system for pushing money out in real time, to a card, bank account or wallet. A business that sends payouts through it has to put money in first, which is called prefunding. Visa said stablecoin prefunding gives clients more flexibility in managing short-term liquidity.

Under the new setup, a client can fund that balance with a stablecoin, a token built to hold a steady value such as one U.S. dollar. Stablecoins move on blockchains around the clock. Triple-A, a Singapore-based stablecoin payments firm, said in a [separate release](https://www.triple-a.io/newsroom/stablecoin-prefunding-visa-direct-asia-pacific) that it handles the conversion, compliance screening and settlement, so payment providers can fund Visa Direct outside traditional banking hours.

Visa said it does not provide regulated digital asset services itself and that a licensed partner handles that side. It did not name which stablecoins the Asia-Pacific pilot will use, and gave no volumes or fees.

**From U.S. Launch to Asia**

Visa began testing stablecoin prefunding in 2025. The service went into commercial use in the U.S. in October with Inyo Global, Visa said, and [The Block](https://www.theblock.co/news/business/2026-11-18-visa-direct-extend-stablecoin-prefunding-cross-border-payouts-asia-pacific-443457) reported that version uses Circle's USDC.

"Asia Pacific already accounts for nearly a third of global cross-border payment flows," Triple-A CEO Eric Barbier said in the release.

Total stablecoin supply stood at $287.8 billion on Wednesday, down $2.59 billion from a week earlier, according to [DefiLlama](https://defillama.com/stablecoins).

*In our opinion: Banks close for the weekend, and blockchains don't, which is the whole pitch here in one sentence. The firms that gain are payout providers that would otherwise wait on a bank wire to top up a balance on a Friday night. The number to watch is how much money actually flows through the pilot, and which stablecoins Visa names when it does.*

articles.title: Fed's Waller Says a Half-Point Hike Is Probably Needed in December
articles.excerpt: Futures price a quarter-point Fed hike on Dec. 9. Waller told CNBC the Fed may need to double that, or spell out a January move, to curb inflation.
articles.body_md:
Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said Wednesday that a half-point interest rate increase is probably needed at the Fed's Dec. 8-9 meeting, telling [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/18/federal-reserve-governor-christopher-waller.html) the central bank "might need to, like, shock people."

Futures already fully price a quarter-point hike in December, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool as cited by CNBC. A half-point move would be double that.

**Waller's Two Options**

Waller said the Fed could instead raise rates by a quarter point and clearly flag another hike in January, either in its statement or at Chairman Kevin Warsh's press conference, [Reuters reported](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/waller-says-on-cnbc-the-fed-needs-to-get-more-aggressive-in-inflation-response-5036212). Without that, he said, "you have to go 50 in December." CNBC noted Warsh has opposed that kind of forward guidance.

"I'm very, very concerned about inflation. It's kind of headed in the wrong direction, and it's spreading out," Waller said. He told the network the Fed needs to reverse its three quarter-point cuts from 2025 and may have to go further.

Reuters reported Waller is worried that businesses now treat 3% inflation as normal and pass it on to customers.

**How a Bigger Hike Reaches Crypto**

The Fed's benchmark rate sets the floor for what cash and short-term Treasuries pay. When that floor rises, assets that pay no interest, such as bitcoin, have to compete with a safer return. Crypto's basis trade, which pays traders for holding bitcoin against short futures, now yields about 3% to 5% a year, near or below Treasury yields, according to Talos data cited by [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/11/18/bitcoin-drops-as-nvidia-earnings-report-drives-stock-index-futures-higher).

Bitcoin traded at $62,311 at 11:47 a.m. ET, down 2.2% over 24 hours, according to CoinGecko.

Not every official agrees. New York Fed President John Williams said Tuesday, "I don't think the situation calls for dramatic action," CNBC reported. The Fed releases minutes of its October meeting at 2 p.m. ET Wednesday.

*In our opinion: The Fed raised rates once in September and held in October, so a half-point move would mark a clear change in pace. Waller's real target is the gap between what markets price and what he thinks is needed. The October minutes due at 2 p.m. ET are the first look at how many colleagues lean his way before the Dec. 9 decision.*

articles.title: UK Inflation Rises to 3.6% as Diesel Hits a Record 199.5p a Litre
articles.excerpt: UK consumer prices rose 3.6% in the year to October, up from 3.5%, as motor fuel costs climbed 33.2%, the ONS said, after this month's Bank of England hike.
articles.body_md:
UK consumer prices rose 3.6% in the 12 months to October, up from 3.5% in September, the [Office for National Statistics](https://www.ons.gov.uk/economy/inflationandpriceindices/bulletins/consumerpriceinflation/october2026) said Wednesday. That matches the rate a year earlier, and the ONS said CPI was last higher in September 2025.

**Fuel Did Most of the Lifting**

Motor fuel prices were 33.2% higher than a year earlier, the biggest annual jump since July 2022, the ONS said. Diesel averaged 199.5 pence a litre in October, the highest since the agency's records began in January 1996. Petrol averaged 174.7 pence, its highest since August 2022.

Restaurants and hotels pulled the other way. Prices there rose 3.4% over the year, down from 3.8% in September, as hotel rates fell.

Core inflation, which strips out energy, food, alcohol and tobacco, was 2.8% and little changed from September. Services inflation held at 3.7%, while goods inflation rose to 3.5% from 3.2%.

**How the Number Is Built**

The Consumer Prices Index (CPI) tracks the cost of a fixed basket of goods and services that households buy, from bread to bus fares. The headline rate compares October's basket with the same month a year earlier. Core inflation removes the most volatile items to show the slower trend underneath.

**What the Bank of England Faces**

The reading matched the forecast of economists polled by Reuters, [CNBC reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/18/uk-inflation-cpi-fuel-prices.html). The Bank of England raised its rate earlier this month for the first time in three years and warned inflation could reach 5% by mid-2027, CNBC said. Traders were pricing about an 80% chance of another hike at the bank's December meeting, according to the same report.

Britain imports more energy than it produces, which leaves it exposed to oil shocks such as the disruption of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, CNBC noted. Oil has eased from wartime highs above $100 a barrel, CNBC said, though it remains elevated.

The ONS publishes November figures on Dec. 16.

*In our opinion: The number that matters is the gap between 3.6% headline inflation and 2.8% core: fuel is doing most of the damage while the slower trend holds steady. Drivers and diesel-heavy businesses carry the cost at nearly 2 pounds a litre. The Bank of England's December decision and the Dec. 16 data will show whether the rate hike becomes a pair.*

articles.title: DBS and Circle Open 24/7 USDC Minting for Asian Institutions
articles.excerpt: DBS said eligible institutional clients in Asia can now mint and redeem Circle's USDC directly through the bank, with dollar settlement around the clock.
articles.body_md:
Singapore's DBS Bank said Wednesday that eligible institutional clients in Asia can mint and redeem Circle's USDC stablecoin directly through the bank, with dollar settlement available 24 hours a day, according to a [joint announcement](https://www.dbs.com/newsroom/DBS_and_Circle_expand_institutional_access_to_USDC_in_Asia).

USDC had about $69.3 billion in circulation as of Wednesday, [The Block reported](https://www.theblock.co/news/business/2026-11-18-dbs-circle-usdc-asia-442970), making it the second-largest stablecoin after Tether's USDT.

**What Minting Through a Bank Means**

A stablecoin is a token meant to hold a steady value, here one U.S. dollar. Minting means handing over dollars and receiving newly created USDC; redeeming is the reverse. Institutions can also buy USDC from other holders on trading venues, which is called the secondary market. DBS said the new route lets clients rely less on that market and move between dollars and USDC outside banking hours and cutoff times.

DBS does not issue the token. USDC is issued by regulated Circle affiliates, and DBS provides the banking side.

**What Was Not Disclosed**

The announcement gave no fees, volumes, client names or list of countries, and did not define which institutions qualify. It said the service targets treasury, settlement and liquidity management.

"By supporting USDC, alongside other trusted tokenised money instruments, we are providing institutions greater choice in how they move and manage value," said Evy Theunis, head of digital assets in DBS's institutional banking group. Circle Chief Commercial Officer Kash Razzaghi said "financial institutions are increasingly looking for trusted ways to access stablecoins."

Both companies take part in Project BLOOM, a Monetary Authority of Singapore effort to make different forms of tokenized money work together. Circle reported that USDC averaged $73.3 billion in circulation in the third quarter, up 8% from a year earlier, The Block said.

*In our opinion: The question worth chasing is volume, and DBS kept that number to itself, which leaves the headline doing most of the work for now. Circle gains a bank on-ramp in Asia at a time when USDC supply is down about $6 billion this year. Watch for the first named clients and markets, and for whether supply moves back toward the $73.3 billion third-quarter average.*
